metadata.title: Relationship Between Neurodevelopmental Areas and Difficulties in Emotional-Behavioural Variables in Children With Typical Development Under 2 Years of Age: Sex Differences
metadata.description: The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between neurodevelopmental areas and possible difficulties in emotional-behavioural variables, and to determine if sex moderated this relationship. A community sample of 231 boys and girls with typical development and with a mean age of 19.84 months was evaluated, using the Bayley-III and CBCL 1.5–5 scales. The main results confirmed: (1) better linguistic abilities in girls in both language areas (receptive communication and expressive communication), finding more evidence according to the Bayesian analysis in expressive communication; (2) in the emotional-behavioural area girls had higher scores in withdrawal; (3) significant negative correlations of low magnitude were found between the Bayley and CBCL scales, particularly in the areas of language and cognitive and internalising and externalising problems; (4) children with low cognitive abilities and those with poor receptive communication showed more inter and externalising difficulties; (5) no significant predictive value or moderating effect of sex was found, (6) the number of participants who simultaneously manifested significant deficits in both domains (neurodevelopmental and emotional-behavioural) was very reduced. Future research should corroborate these results and the characteristics of the relationship found at these early ages. Detecting the population at risk in the first two years of life would enable the implementation of interventions aimed at improving neurodevelopmental deficits and emotional-behavioural problems. Thus, identification of deficits in one domain should lead to evaluation of the other.

metadata.title: Economie sociale et solidaire : cadre conceptuel et fondements théoriques
metadata.description:
Résumé 

Cet article analyse le cadre conceptuel et les fondements théoriques de l’économie sociale et solidaire (ESS), désormais reconnue comme un paradigme central du développement inclusif et durable. En mobilisant une approche à la fois historique et analytique, l’étude retrace l’évolution de la pensée relative à l’ESS, depuis les théoriciens classiques du XIXᵉ siècle, tels que Walras, Gide, Owen et Fourier, jusqu’aux approches contemporaines développées par Desroche, Vienney, Laville, Lévesque et Mendell. L’analyse met en évidence les principes fondamentaux qui distinguent l’ESS de l’économie marchande traditionnelle : la gouvernance démocratique, la primauté de la finalité sociale sur le capital et la solidarité collective. Dans le contexte marocain, l’article situe l’institutionnalisation de l’ESS au cœur des politiques publiques, notamment à travers l’Initiative Nationale pour le Développement Humain (2005) et le Nouveau Modèle de Développement (2021). Les résultats révèlent le caractère hybride et pluriel de l’ESS, à l’intersection des logiques marchande, non marchande et non monétaire, ainsi que sa capacité à promouvoir l’innovation sociale et l’inclusion économique. En définitive, cette recherche contribue à une meilleure compréhension de l’ESS en tant que modèle alternatif susceptible de concilier performance économique, justice sociale et durabilité.

Mots clés : économie sociale et solidaire, gouvernance démocratique, innovation sociale, développement inclusif, durabilité, Maroc.

Classification JEL : L31, O35, Z13, P13.

Type du papier : Recherche Théorique.

 

Abstract

This article examines the conceptual framework and theoretical foundations of the Social and Solidarity Economy (SSE), considered today as a key paradigm for inclusive and sustainable development. By mobilizing a historical and analytical approach, the study explores the evolution of SSE thought from the classical theorists of the 19th century, such as Walras, Gide, Owen, and Fourier to contemporary approaches developed by Desroche, Vienney, Laville, Lévesque, and Mendell. The analysis highlights the main principles that distinguish SSE from the traditional market economy: democratic governance, primacy of social purpose over capital, and collective solidarity. In the Moroccan context, the article situates the institutionalization of SSE within public policies, notably through the National Initiative for Human Development (2005) and the New Development Model (2021). The results underscore the hybrid and plural nature of SSE, located at the intersection of market, non-market, and non-monetary logics, and its capacity to promote social innovation and economic inclusion. Ultimately, the research contributes to a better understanding of SSE as an alternative model capable of reconciling economic performance, social justice, and sustainability.

 

Keywords: Social and Solidarity Economy, democratic governance, social innovation, inclusive development, sustainability, Morocco.

JEL Classification: L31, O35, Z13, P13.

Paper type: Theoretical Research.

metadata.title: PGSD Eccentricity Demonstration Reproducibility Package v1.1
metadata.description:
Version 1.1 - corrected reference-sphere geometry

This repository provides the data, analysis code, numerical outputs, and documentation required to reproduce the center-eccentricity demonstration presented in the manuscript:

“Physics-Guided Scientific Discovery (PGSD): A Reference Architecture for Explainable Knowledge Generation in Mechanical Engineering.”

Version 1.1 supersedes version 1.0. It corrects the reference-sphere diameter from 24.9984 mm to 24.98484 mm and consequently updates the effective probe-center contact radius to:

R_e = 15.49242 mm.

The original CNC measurement files are preserved unchanged. The correction affects the contact-geometry constants, the constant-radius interpretation, and the calculated higher-order contact scale. It does not change the first-order LFH differential coefficient pair because those coefficients are estimated from the measured-coordinate columns and angular directions.

The demonstration uses two CNC touch-probing acquisitions of the reference sphere, denoted X0Y0 and LT_X0Y0, each containing 32 equatorial measurement points. A nominal relative offset of (-0.300, -0.300) mm was introduced through the CNC/G54 command between the two acquisitions.

The package includes:

  • the original CNC measurement files in CMM format;
  • normalized coordinate datasets;
  • Python scripts for Local Fourier Harmonic analysis and circle fitting;
  • numerical results corresponding to the manuscript;
  • files used to reproduce Figure 4;
  • documentation of the coordinate convention, units, sampling sequence, contact-geometry constants, and execution procedure;
  • a version history and correction note;
  • a package manifest and SHA-256 checksums.

The package reproduces the first-order LFH differential coefficient pair:

  • Delta a1 = -0.299865 mm
  • Delta b1 = -0.300743 mm

and the corresponding provisional inferred magnitude of 0.424695 mm. Using the corrected effective contact radius, the characteristic second-order contact scale is 2.90465 micrometres.

The nominal CNC/G54-commanded offset was not independently measured using an external calibrated displacement reference. Therefore, the numerical differences between the LFH estimate and the nominal command must not be interpreted as independently verified displacement errors. Only one acquisition was available for each state, and no complete uncertainty budget, within-state repeatability study, or multi-state validation was performed. The reported coefficient pair is consequently classified as a physically and operationally corroborated Candidate Signature, not as a validated or canonical Signature.

Changes from version 1.0

  • corrected the reference-sphere diameter to 24.98484 mm;
  • updated the effective contact radius to 15.49242 mm;
  • updated the higher-order contact-scale calculation to 2.90465 micrometres;
  • updated the analysis documentation, numerical metadata, and checksums;
  • preserved the original CMM measurement files;
  • confirmed that the first-order LFH differential coefficients and provisional inverse estimate remain unchanged.

This package supports Section 6 of the PGSD Foundation Preprint v1.2.

metadata.title: The Influence of Folk Art on Contemporary Artistic and Design Practices
metadata.description:
Abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of folk art and crafts on modern design practices. It will focus on how designers can find innovative ways to apply folk art aesthetic, design languages to evolve and integrate new design languages. The second aspect is how designers can take advantage of technology to achieve desired effects without disturbing the traditional values of the folk arts and crafts. Folk art is deeply rooted in the cultural essence of a region, profoundly influenced by its soil, nature, and geographical characteristics. The close connection between people and their environment is evident in their artistic expressions, where bold and straightforward forms reflect their intrinsic bond with nature. This connection is further exemplified in their vibrant use of colors, linear depictions, and decorative motifs that breathe life into their homes, attire, and everyday objects. The graphic qualities of folk art—its simplicity, charm, and directness—remain fascinating and captivating.
India boasts a rich and diverse tradition of folk art and craft. Each region’s artistic expressions mirror the country’s cultural diversity, shaped by the distinct geographical features of its provinces. Folk art and craft are inseparable from the daily lives of the people, intricately linked to their festivals, rituals, and seasonal changes, which are often tied to agricultural and religious practices. These art forms embody the rhythm of life, weaving together nature and human activity.
For artists and designers, this vibrant lifestyle and its associated art forms—such as dance, music, textiles, pottery, cane work, and geometric crafts—offer a wealth of inspiration. These folk traditions present unique opportunities for exploring functionality, aesthetics, and decoration. The simplification of forms and motifs, particularly of animals, birds, and flora, often serves as a creative foundation for modern interpretations.
This study delves into the inspirational impact of folk art on contemporary artists and illustrators, many of whom have formal training in modern or academic art. Despite their backgrounds, these creators often integrate elements of tribal and folk art into their work, blending these influences with their unique design sensibilities to produce innovative artistic expressions. By analyzing these works, this study uncovers how folk-art traditions resonate within modern creative practices and explores the artistic parameters that define this interaction.
In addition to artistic creations, designers and illustrators have found innovative ways to apply folk aesthetics in communication design. The influence of folk art is evident in advertising, publication design, environmental graphics, outdoor publicity, and editorial illustrations. These contemporary applications demonstrate the enduring relevance of folk aesthetics, as they resonate strongly with the cultural psyche, creating a sense of “Indian-ness” that connects with people across social strata and popular culture. The impact of folk art extends beyond individual creations, influencing the broader field of design education. By studying how artists and designers adapt folk aesthetics, we can identify key inspirational elements that inform modern teaching methodologies.
Practical Implications: Practical exercises based on these findings can be integrated into contemporary design education, fostering a deeper appreciation of folk traditions while equipping students with innovative tools for creative expression. The approach of this study encourages the continuation of folk art’s legacy, ensuring its relevance in modern artistic and design practices. The study not only highlights the cultural significance of these traditions but also offers a roadmap for their integration into the evolving landscape of art and design.

metadata.title: Structural Mechanisms of Collision Dependence in Constructibility Jacobians
metadata.description:
For polynomial observables of a fixed resonance-free discrete dynamical system, we ask when
a coefficient map’s generic Jacobian rank can be certified independently of any particular pa-
rameter value. We prove that a family is immune to special-parameter rank deficiency whenever
it admits a full-rank Jacobian minor built entirely from collision-free coefficients, and we identify
two distinct mechanisms by which this immunity can fail. The first is dimensional: when the
minimal coefficient count equals the state dimension, the Jacobian has a unique minor, forcing
collision dependence whenever any coefficient is collision-dependent. The second is algebraic:
even when several candidate collision-free minors exist, they may be constrained to an alge-
braic variety of positive codimension, forcing rank deficiency independently of dimension count.
We establish this second mechanism via a discriminant-type identity among coefficients and a
general chain-rule bound, and verify both mechanisms against every family examined in a com-
panion paper, yielding a complete structural classification. Two simple explanatory hypotheses
considered in that companion paper – that collision count, or the number of shared algebraic fac-
tors, alone determines rank behaviour – are shown to be insufficient; For the analysed families,
structural forcing is the only criterion found to separate every family correctly.

data.title: Structural Mechanisms of Collision Dependence in Constructibility Jacobians

metadata.title: PCC-Explorer
metadata.description:
PCC-Explorer is an open-source software tool to assess the impact of GNSS antenna Phase Center Corrections (PCC) on geodetic parameters.

PCC-Explorer allows researchers and practitioners to analyze how PCC differences propagate into estimated geodetic parameters
such as coordinates and tropospheric delays.

metadata.title: Daily DML-Sat Multi-Model Ensemble Mean Dataset of Equivalent Black Carbon in Snow over Northern Xinjiang, China
metadata.description:
This dataset provides daily, 500 m multi-model ensemble mean estimates of equivalent black carbon in snow (eBCsnow) over northern Xinjiang, Northwest China. The dataset was generated using DML-Sat, a physically and observationally constrained dual machine-learning framework. Here, eBCsnow is defined as the black carbon concentration required to reproduce the optical snow-darkening effect caused by light-absorbing particles in snow.

DML-Sat consists of two components. DML-Sat_A learns the physically consistent relationships among snow spectral reflectance, eBCsnow concentration, snow grain size, and snow cover fraction from SNICAR radiative-transfer simulations. Four snow-grain morphologies and two black-carbon mixing states are considered, producing eight physical configurations. The trained models are driven by daily MODIS/Terra MOD09GA seven-band surface reflectance and solar zenith angle to generate preliminary eBCsnow estimates.

DML-Sat_B subsequently uses field observations from Northwest China to correct systematic biases in the preliminary estimates. Uncertainties from field measurements and MODIS inputs are propagated through a Monte Carlo calibration procedure. Four machine-learning algorithms—Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost—with two configurations for each algorithm are used to represent model structural uncertainty.

For each valid MODIS pixel, eight observation-corrected estimates are generated, and their ensemble mean is used as the final eBCsnow concentration. The dataset can support studies of snow-darkening variability, snow-albedo reduction, radiative forcing, snowmelt acceleration, and the influences of anthropogenic emissions and natural dust sources.

dates.description: Temporal coverage of daily DML-Sat data from October 2000 to April 2025. Data are provided only for October–April in each snow season.

metadata.title: ULTR-AI: Ultrasound-led TB Recognition Using AI
metadata.description: ULTR-AI is research software for developing and evaluating artificial intelligence models that analyze lung ultrasound for pulmonary tuberculosis triage. The codebase supports direct image-to-TB prediction, prediction of human-recognizable lung ultrasound signs, patient-level aggregation, and evaluation against study outcome labels.
